questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some goats are eagles.

All eagles are snakes.

No duck is an eagle.

**Conclusions:**

(I) No snake is a goat.

(II) Some ducks are snakes is a possibility.

(III) Some ducks are not goats

options.text: Both conclusions II and III follow
Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1449eb76a4712ca3448d911f3f79a59717f764aaffe5bd59b61b2df02eadec21.png] 

Conclusions:

I. No snake is a goat → Does not Follow (As, some goats are eagles and all eagles are snakes, So, it is possible but not definitely true)

II. Some ducks are snakes is a possibility → Follow (As, no duck is an eagle and all eagles are snakes. and, no definite relation is given between snakes and duck, so some ducks are snakes can be possible therefore it is definitely true)

III. Some ducks are not goats → Does not Follow (As, some goats are eagles, all eagles are snakes and no duck is an eagle. So, no definite relation is given between goats and duck, so some ducks are not goats can be possible but not definitely true)

Here, Only conclusion II follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Only conclusion II follows".

**Statements:**

All flowers are trees.

All branches are leaves.

No flowers are leaves.

**Conclusions:**

(I) No branches are flowers.

(II) No trees are leaves.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8001f0cefa233b9ef5a2e4f8b2537adbd5fc7a31f89e2e0dea4f918c511f797f.png] 

Conclusions:

I. No branches are flowers → Follow (As, all branches are leaves and no flowers are leaves, So, whole branches comes in leaves which cannot be flowers therefore it is definitely true.)

II. No trees are leaves → **Does not Follow** (As, all flowers are trees and, no flowers are leaves all branches are leaves. and, no definite relation is given between trees and leaves, so No trees are leaves can be possible but not definitely true)

Here, Only conclusion (I) follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Only conclusion (I) follows".

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All beans are meat

All breads are meat

**Conclusions:**

I. Some beans are breads.

II. Some breads are beans.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Either conclusion I or II follows
Neither conclusion I nor II follows

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/348f982b0f11da79622a28648c7ff0060dd4610e466d7b8200b60c592ba2a0d8.png] 

Concept:

1) We have to check the conclusions are 100% match with the statement. If the conclusion is 100% match with the given statement then the conclusion is true. If there is a 1% chance of not following the statement then the conclusion is considered to be false.

2) The possibility case can be considered to be "false" in "definite case".

3) In Possibility case, either "can" or "possible" word must be present.

The least possible Venn diagram is,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/17352670d85d48700b802c94e430c4f7c4c6a2d816ceb3c370e5d19263213044.png] 

Conclusion I: Some beans are breads → False (This is possible but not definite)

Conclusion II: Some breads are beans → False (This is possible but not definite)

Hence, neither conclusion I nor II follows

Note: 

Conditions of Either-or case:

1. The elements should be the same in both the statements.

2. Individually both the conclusions should be false.

3. One conclusion should be positive and one conclusion should be negative (Complementary pair)

The two complementary pairs are:

1) All + Some not

2) No + Some
